title: EV-18 TimerDue changes direction and owner between Event and Messaging Design v4 and Architecture v5
source: Recovery Workbench Event and Messaging Design v4; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1
section: Event and Messaging Design v4, sheet Events, row EV-18; Architecture v5 slide 42 row 18; Ownership Map, sheet Events, row EV-18
description: Version 4 publishes TimerDue from the Case and workflow module to a Rules component. Architecture v5 slide 42 row 18 gives the producer as a durable timer, gives no topic and marks the event retired, because the timer lives inside the workflow; the Ownership Map follows Architecture v5 and records PLT as the owner. Both cannot stand: either TimerDue is a rwb-case event on rwb.case.events.v1, or it is retired and the clock is a durable Temporal timer. No source states which of the two is in force for the build.
evidence: Event and Messaging Design v4 cell A22: 'EV-18 | TimerDue | Published | Case and workflow | timerId, caseId, timerType | Rules component'. Architecture v5 slide 42 row 18: 'TimerDue | durable timer | - | (retired: timer inside the workflow)'. Ownership Map sheet Events row EV-18 owner PLT with the ruling that TimerDue is not a rwb-case event type.
proposed: Confirm that TimerDue is retired, that no TimerDue event type is provisioned, and that the timer is a durable Temporal timer inside CaseWorkflow; TimerBreached (EV-19) then stays the only timer event on rwb.case.events.v1.

title: EV-21 PartnerResultSubmitted is consumed in v4 and published by rwb-partner in Architecture v5
source: Recovery Workbench Event and Messaging Design v4; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1
section: Event and Messaging Design v4, sheet Events, row EV-21; Architecture v5 slide 43 row 21; Ownership Map, sheet Events, row EV-21
description: Version 4 marks PartnerResultSubmitted as Consumed with the owning module Partner portal, so the event enters the Workbench from outside. Architecture v5 slide 43 row 21 gives rwb-partner as the producer, with rwb-litigation, rwb-asset and rwb-case as consumers. The direction of the event and the owner of the event type therefore differ between the two sources.
evidence: Event and Messaging Design v4 cell A25: 'EV-21 | PartnerResultSubmitted | Consumed | Partner portal | instructionId, result, documents | Case and workflow'. Architecture v5 slide 43 row 21: 'PartnerResultSubmitted | rwb-partner | rwb.partner.events.v1 | rwb-litigation, rwb-asset, rwb-case'. Ownership Map sheet Events row EV-21 owner S9 with the ruling that the partner portal is the external channel into rwb-partner.
proposed: Confirm that rwb-partner publishes PartnerResultSubmitted on rwb.partner.events.v1 when the partner result arrives, with rwb-litigation, rwb-asset and rwb-case as consumers, and that the partner portal is a channel into rwb-partner and not the owner of the event type.

title: EV-26 AceDataReady is consumed in v4 and published by rwb-source-data in Architecture v5
source: Recovery Workbench Event and Messaging Design v4; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1
section: Event and Messaging Design v4, sheet Events, row EV-26; Architecture v5 slide 43 row 26; Ownership Map, sheet Events, row EV-26
description: Version 4 marks AceDataReady as Consumed, owned by ACE ingestion and read through v_ace_batch_status. Architecture v5 slide 43 row 26 gives rwb-source-data as the producer and lists rwb-case, rwb-payment, rwb-deviation and rwb-writeoff as consumers. ACE ingestion is outside the 19 services, so the event cannot be consumed from it in the target: rwb-source-data reads the ACE batch record and publishes the event.
evidence: Event and Messaging Design v4 cell A30: 'EV-26 | AceDataReady | Consumed | ACE ingestion, read through v_ace_batch_status | sourceSystem (source_system), businessDate (business_date), status, completedAt (completed_at)'. Architecture v5 slide 43 row 26: 'AceDataReady | rwb-source-data | rwb.source-data.events.v1 | rwb-case, rwb-payment, rwb-deviation, rwb-writeoff'. Ownership Map sheet Events row EV-26 owner P1.
proposed: Confirm that rwb-source-data publishes AceDataReady on rwb.source-data.events.v1 after reading recovery.v_ace_batch_status, that ACE ingestion stays outside the 19 services, and that the read of the view is not written to the outbox under the Transactions rule.

title: No retry topic name is given for any event topic
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; RWB-PLT-N002-INF Kafka topics, retry and dead-letter topics and ACLs
section: Architecture v5 slide 9 (Kafka settings), slide 22 (the event path); RWB-PLT-N002-INF section 11
description: Architecture v5 fixes three retry windows, 1 min, 10 min and 1 h, and says that a record then goes to '.dlt', but it names no retry topic. RWB-PLT-N002-INF counts three retry topics per event topic, 60 in the set, and records the naming as an open point of the platform story. The topic catalogue can therefore give the count, the window of each retry topic and its owner, but not the name of a single retry topic.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 9: 'retry 1 min, 10 min, 1 h then .dlt'. Architecture v5 slide 22 lists 'retry 1 min', 'retry 10 min', 'retry 1 h', '.dlt + alert'. RWB-PLT-N002-INF section 11 and section 12.9 state 60 retry topics and record the derived names as not specified in the source documents.
proposed: Agree the retry topic naming rule with the ACE platform team and write it into the topic catalogue: three retry topics per event topic, one per window, derived from the event topic name so that no service story has to invent a name.

title: No dead-letter topic name, partition count or retention is given
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; RWB-PLT-N002-INF Kafka topics, retry and dead-letter topics and ACLs
section: Architecture v5 slide 9 (Kafka settings), slide 22 (the event path); RWB-PLT-N002-INF section 11
description: Architecture v5 says a record that fails the three retry windows goes to '.dlt' with an alert, and RWB-PLT-N002-INF says one dead-letter topic per event topic with the same partition count. Neither source states the full dead-letter topic name, its replication factor or its retention, so the 20 dead-letter topics of the set are named in this catalogue by the suffix the source gives and their settings are recorded as open.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 9: 'retry 1 min, 10 min, 1 h then .dlt'. Architecture v5 slide 22: '.dlt + alert'. RWB-PLT-N002-INF AC2: 'one dead-letter topic with the same partition count'. No source names a dead-letter topic or gives its retention.
proposed: Agree the dead-letter topic name, replication factor, retention and replay window with the ACE platform team, and provision the 20 dead-letter topics from the same configuration file as the event topics.

title: The shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1 has no settings of its own in any source
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; RWB-PLT-N002-INF Kafka topics, retry and dead-letter topics and ACLs
section: Architecture v5 slides 9, 20 and 42 row 08; RWB-PLT-N002-INF section 11
description: Architecture v5 gives partitions, replication, retention and key for 'topic per service rwb.<name>.events.v1' only. The shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1 carries DecisionRecorded from all 19 services, but no source gives it a partition count, a replication factor, a retention or a key of its own.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 9: 'topic per service rwb.<name>.events.v1, 12 partitions, replication factor 3, 7-day retention, key caseId'. Slide 42 row 08 puts DecisionRecorded on rwb.decision-record.v1 with all 19 as producer. No source states the settings of the shared topic.
proposed: Confirm that the shared topic takes the same settings as the service topics, 12 partitions, replication factor 3, 7-day retention and key caseId, or state the settings that differ.

title: The v4 failure rule sends a failed event to an exception queue, the target sends it to a dead-letter topic
source: Recovery Workbench Event and Messaging Design v4; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1
section: Event and Messaging Design v4, sheet Rules, row Failure; Architecture v5 slide 22 (the event path)
description: The v4 rule reads that after the retry limit 'the event goes to the exception queue with its owner'. The target has no exception queue: a record walks three retry topics and then a dead-letter topic with an alert and a replay tool. The same words cannot describe both, so the rule is carried into v5 with the dead-letter reading.
evidence: Event and Messaging Design v4 sheet Rules row Failure: 'A consumer failure retries; after the limit the event goes to the exception queue with its owner'. Architecture v5 slide 22: 'retry 1 min', 'retry 10 min', 'retry 1 h', '.dlt + alert'; slide 9: 'retry 1 min, 10 min, 1 h then .dlt'.
proposed: Confirm that the exception queue of v4 is the dead-letter topic of the target, that the owner named by the rule is the producing service, and that the alert and the replay tool are the recovery path.

title: The 15 event types named only in the Architecture v5 service catalogue have no payload
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Event and Messaging Design v4
section: Architecture v5 slide 41 service catalogue slides (one EVT line per service); Event and Messaging Design v4, sheet Events
description: Fifteen event types are named on the service catalogue slides of Architecture v5 and have no row in the v4 event table, so no payload is stated for them: ApprovalDecided, ReportPublished, FileDelivered, FileFailed, RouteDecided, TreatmentClosed, GuaranteeClaimFiled, GuaranteeClaimSettled, LawsuitFiled, JudgmentRecorded, AuctionResult, AssetSold, AccountsTransferred, AccessPolicyChanged and DoaLimitChanged. The payload of these types cannot be given without inventing fields.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 41 service catalogue lines, for example 'EVT rwb.decision.events.v1: ApprovalRequested, ApprovalDecided, RulePackageInForce', 'EVT rwb.reporting.events.v1: ReportPublished', 'EVT rwb.litigation.events.v1: LawsuitFiled, JudgmentRecorded, AuctionResult'. Event and Messaging Design v4 sheet Events holds EV-01 to EV-30 only.
proposed: Fix the payload of each of the 15 event types in the CON story of the owning service, with IDs and codes only and no personal data, and register the schema before the first consumer is built.

title: No consumer is given for ApprovalDecided, ReportPublished or LawsuitFiled
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1
description: Slides 42 and 43 give the consumer services of every event they list, except for these three types: ApprovalDecided and LawsuitFiled appear on the service catalogue slides only, and ReportPublished is named on the rwb-reporting line with no consumer at all. The read side of these three types therefore cannot be stated, so neither can their read ACL.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 41 service catalogue: 'EVT rwb.reporting.events.v1: ReportPublished' with no consumer line; ApprovalDecided and LawsuitFiled appear only in the topic lists 'rwb.decision.events.v1: ApprovalRequested, ApprovalDecided, RulePackageInForce' and 'rwb.litigation.events.v1: LawsuitFiled, JudgmentRecorded, AuctionResult'. Slides 42 and 43 list no row for the three.
proposed: Confirm the consumers of ApprovalDecided, ReportPublished and LawsuitFiled, and grant the read ACL from that list only.

title: No registry subject and no JSON Schema is named per event type
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; RWB-PLT-N008-INF Schema registry with BACKWARD compatibility
section: Architecture v5 slide 9 (JSON Schema registry with BACKWARD compatibility), slide 22 (schemas versioned in the registry)
description: Architecture v5 requires a JSON Schema registry with BACKWARD compatibility and an AsyncAPI document per service, but no source names a subject, a schema file or a schema version for any of the 43 event types. This catalogue can name the event type, the topic and the payload field list of the 28 types that v4 states, and nothing more.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 9: 'JSON Schema registry with BACKWARD compatibility'; slide 22: 'Schemas are versioned in the registry with BACKWARD compatibility; the AsyncAPI document per service is the contract'. Event and Messaging Design v4 rule Versioning: 'An event carries its schema version; consumers accept the current and previous version'. No subject name appears in either source.
proposed: Agree the subject naming rule in the registry story, register the schema of each event type before its first publish, and record the subject and the version in this catalogue in its next version.

title: The values of ce_source and ce_subject are not stated
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1
section: Architecture v5 slide 22 (CloudEvents 1.0 binary mode headers)
description: Architecture v5 names the CloudEvents binary-mode headers ce_id, ce_type, ce_source and ce_subject and fixes the record key as caseId, but it gives no value form for ce_source and ce_subject. The envelope of this design therefore states the header names, the requirement that ce_type follows rwb.<short>.<Event>.v1 and ce_id is the event identity, and leaves the two values to the naming library.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 22: 'CloudEvents 1.0 Kafka binding in binary mode: ce_id, ce_type, ce_source, ce_subject as headers, W3C traceparent header, JSON body validated against the registry'. Slide 9: 'key caseId'. No value form for ce_source or ce_subject appears.
proposed: Agree the value form of ce_source and ce_subject in the event naming library RWB-PLT-E1047-CON, and apply it uniformly in every producer.

title: The idempotency key of an event is required but its derivation is not stated
source: Recovery Workbench Event and Messaging Design v4; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1
section: Event and Messaging Design v4, sheet Rules, row Duplicates; Architecture v5 slide 22 (inbox table processed_event)
description: The v4 rule requires each event to carry an event ID and an idempotency key, and a repeat to be ignored and counted. Architecture v5 states that each consumer records ce_id in its inbox table in the same transaction as its own change, and says nothing about a second key. The derivation of the idempotency key is therefore unstated, and the outbox and inbox of the target need one rule.
evidence: Event and Messaging Design v4 sheet Rules row Duplicates: 'Each event carries an event ID and an idempotency key; a repeat is ignored and counted (R-UNI-40)'. Architecture v5 slide 22: 'Each records ce_id in its inbox table (processed_event) in the same transaction as its own change'. No source derives a separate idempotency key.
proposed: Confirm that the idempotency key of an event is its ce_id, that the inbox table processed_event holds ce_id as its key, and that the duplicate count of R-UNI-40 is taken from the inbox.
